title: Add three string-analysis functions to Rust string-utils: is_palindrome, count_vowels, slugify
description: A Rust string-utils library needs three new string-analysis functions with tests.

task_spec.prompt:
The Rust library in src/lib.rs has word_count and capitalize_words. Add three new functions:

1. pub fn is_palindrome(s: &str) -> bool
   Returns true if s (ignoring case and non-alphabetic chars) reads the same forwards and backwards.
   Examples: is_palindrome("racecar") == true, is_palindrome("A man a plan a canal Panama") == true, is_palindrome("hello") == false.

2. pub fn count_vowels(s: &str) -> usize
   Returns the number of ASCII vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) in s.
   Examples: count_vowels("Hello World") == 3, count_vowels("") == 0.

3. pub fn slugify(s: &str) -> String
   Converts s to a URL slug: lowercase, non-alphanumeric chars replaced by hyphens, consecutive hyphens collapsed to one, leading/trailing hyphens removed.
   Examples: slugify("Hello World!") == "hello-world", slugify("  Rust is Great  ") == "rust-is-great".

Add 2 tests per function (6 total). All 3 existing tests must still pass.
cargo test must show 9+ tests passing. cargo build must succeed.
success_criteria: is_palindrome ignores case and non-alpha chars
followup_prompts: Good. Now add input validation and error handling to the feature you just implemented. What should happen with invalid, missing, or malformed inputs? Update the implementation and tests to cover those cases.
Run `cargo test` to verify everything including your new error handling. Fix any failures and confirm the feature is complete.
